label: 3rd/4th input step when the input is one of u,d,o,0,c,f,2,b,q (or <DEL> at L=3)
explanation: Position-plus-token unit. It fires only at steps t=2 and t=3 (the third and fourth inputs; t=4 holds under 1% of mass) and never in the copy phase. At those positions it is selective for the input token: u is strongest (the top activations are all u at t=3), then d, o, 0, c, f, 2, with weaker b and q. It also fires on <DEL> when <DEL> lands at t=3 (L=3). Within that set, activations are lower when the token repeats an earlier input. It does not fire at t=0, 1, or t>=5, or on any copy step. Other tokens at t=2/3 (e.g. a, 3, h) sometimes give weak activations, which accounts for most of the missed recall.

issues: Core facts hold. Activity is almost entirely at t=2 (56% of activation mass) and t=3 (43%). t=4 holds 0.9% of the mass, there is zero activity at t=0, t=1, t>=5 or in the copy phase, and <DEL> at t=3 fires with precision 0.72. The reported test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.791, R 0.754, F1 0.772, mass recall 0.883).

The token set is a graded ranking, not a clean category. Precision at t=2 / t=3 by token: u 1.00/0.995, d 0.999/0.96, o 0.975/0.86, 0 0.96/0.78, c 0.90/0.67, f 0.86/0.64, 2 0.83/0.59, b 0.69/0.46, q 0.64/0.39, 3 0.45/0.25, a 0.44/0.27, h/j/i/p/w about 0.2-0.32. b and q (0.39-0.46 at t=3) are barely separable from a and 3, which were excluded. The cutoff is therefore arbitrary, and the label overstates how crisp the token set is.

There is a systematic missed context effect that the explanation never mentions: the previous input token strongly modulates activation. For the borderline tokens (a, 3, b, q, h, j, i, p) at t=2/3, precision ranges from 0.04-0.18 when prev_tok is 3, q, p, b, v, l, s, 1 or z up to 0.58-0.76 when prev_tok is 0, w, y, j or r. Many of the false positives (b, q, 3 after a suppressing prev token) and missed activations (a, h, j, p after a boosting prev token) follow this pattern rather than being scattered noise. The unit looks like an additive weighting of current and previous tokens, gated to t=2/3.
The explanation's account of repeats (activations are lower when a token repeats an earlier input) is weak in the data. For a at t=2, precision is 0.437 on first occurrence and 0.474 on repeat.
A predicate that adds the previous-token context reaches test F1 0.801 (P 0.793, R 0.810, mass recall 0.913), compared with 0.772 for the original. That puts it over the 0.8 bar the original missed.
